title: I Feel Frustrated
can_do: 说出找不到拼图块带来的沮丧，请求帮助，并在一起找到后报告感受的变化。

conversation_move.label: name a feeling and its reason

trigger: The last puzzle piece is missing. Child explains his frustration with because, and Mom's clue leads him to the blue piece under the table.
setting: Finishing a simple puzzle together at a low table at home.
essential_props: one four-piece puzzle with its final blue piece under the low table

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: One last puzzle piece is missing.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: I'm frustrated because I can't find it.

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: I understand. You worked hard on this puzzle.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: Yes. Three pieces were easy. The last one is hiding.

turns.speaker: mom
turns.line: Let's look under the low table.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: The blue piece! It was under the table.

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: It fits! I feel better now.

replay_cards.title: The torn picture
replay_cards.change: The edge of Child's nearly finished picture tears as he moves it
replay_cards.challenge: Child explains, "I'm frustrated because I worked hard on it." Mom acknowledges the effort and asks whether help or a pause would be useful. Child requests "Can we stop? I need a break." Mom leaves the picture safe; after a real pause, Child chooses to tape the edge with her and continue drawing. He can remain disappointed while accepting help.

replay_cards.title: The missed turn
replay_cards.setting: A family board game with Dad
replay_cards.change: Dad accidentally takes two turns, then mistakes Child's complaint for a request to go next
replay_cards.challenge: Child says, "You skipped my turn." Dad asks, "Do you mean you want the next turn?" Child corrects, "No, I mean you skipped my turn." Dad acknowledges the mistake and moves his piece back. Child proposes "First my turn, then your turn." Dad agrees; Child takes the restored turn, then Dad takes his, and they continue without requiring Child to cheer up first.

parent_support: Accept the small frown and pause as meaningful frustration. Acknowledge the missing piece before suggesting a search; do not turn the feeling into a quiz.
Help after Child asks, check just one reachable place together, and let finding the piece explain the slight relief. A smile is optional, and another situation may need a real break.
